one_liner: Zero-allocation Go UAX #29 grapheme/word/sentence segmenter (Unicode 17); 14x rivo/uniseg graphemes, 3.6x blevesearch/segment words, first-party.
what_it_does: Splits UTF-8 text into grapheme clusters, words, phrases or sentences under the default Unicode 17 UAX #29 rules. Each package offers FromString, FromBytes (generic iterators with Next/Value/Start/End/Reset/SetText/First), FromReader (an embedded bufio.Scanner) and a bufio.SplitFunc. Tokens are subslices of the input, so nothing is copied. The words package returns every segment, including spaces and punctuation, and optional Joiners keep characters such as - / @ # inside words. The graphemes iterator can also treat 7-bit and 8-bit ECMA-48 escape sequences as single clusters.
how_it_is_fast: Break properties come from generated tries indexed directly by UTF-8 bytes, so a lookup needs no rune decoding. The rules run as one forward pass that carries the last two non-ignored properties, a regional-indicator count and a three-state GB9c (Indic conjunct) tracker, so it never looks back. ASCII fast paths in Next() (PR #42, January 2026) skip the rule engine: an ASCII byte other than CR followed by another ASCII byte or end of text is a grapheme by itself, and a run of [A-Za-z0-9] followed by an ASCII space or end of text is a word. Both shortcuts are correct under UAX #29, since no ASCII character is Extend, SpacingMark, Prepend or regional indicator. Iterators are generic over string and []byte and report 0 allocs/op.
when_to_use: Go search and NLP pipelines (inverted indexes, BM25, embedding chunking) that need standard UAX #29 word tokens: 212 MB/s multilingual and 282 MB/s ASCII prose on an Apple M2, with no allocations.
Grapheme-correct cursor movement, truncation or counting in Go TUIs and CLIs; clipperhouse/displaywidth and the Charm stack build on it.
ASCII-heavy or mostly-Latin text, where the fast paths apply on almost every byte (509 MB/s graphemes on a repeated ASCII pangram).
Terminal output carrying colour codes: AnsiEscapeSequences keeps each escape sequence as one token, checked against charmbracelet/x/ansi's DecodeSequence in the comparative tests.
Streaming input via FromReader/SplitFunc with bufio.Scanner, or text already in memory as string or []byte with no conversion.
when_not_to_use: When you also need line-break (UAX #14) opportunities or monospace width per cluster: rivo/uniseg's Step returns graphemes, words, sentences, line breaks and width in one pass. uax29 has no line breaking (issue #50 closed), and width lives in the separate displaywidth package.

Language-tailored word segmentation (Thai, Lao, Khmer, Chinese and Japanese dictionary breaking): only the default UAX #29 rules are implemented, so ideographs and Southeast Asian scripts are not split into dictionary words.
Untrusted input that may be invalid UTF-8: the README calls the result undefined (garbage in, garbage out); fuzzing guards only against panics and infinite loops, so validate with utf8.Valid first.

Pipelines that rely on blevesearch/segment token types (Letter, Number, Kana, Ideo) or its exact boundaries: uax29 words returns untyped tokens, and the harness itself notes that counts can differ from blevesearch.
Non-Go code: this is a pure Go module. The C# port (clipperhouse/uax29.net) is separate, and for C/C++ the catalogued alternatives are libgrapheme, uni-algo and ICU.

integration.form: module (pure-Go packages: graphemes, words, phrases, sentences)
integration.dependencies: none (root go.mod has no require lines; the comparative benchmark modules pull rivo/uniseg v0.4.7, blevesearch/segment v0.9.1 and charmbracelet/x/ansi v0.11.6)
integration.min_toolchain: go.mod declares go 1.18 (generics); CI only tests Go 1.21-1.26 with -race -short. PR #42 described a bump to 1.20 that HEAD's go.mod does not show.
integration.platforms: any GOOS/GOARCH (no assembly or unsafe in the iterator and split code read); the published benchmarks ran on darwin/arm64
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. An Iterator is a small mutable struct, so give each goroutine its own; the SplitFunc and generated tables are read-only and safe to share.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false: a different API from uniseg (NewGraphemes/Next/Str, Step with boundary flags) and blevesearch/segment (NewWordSegmenter/Segment/Bytes/Type); FromReader and SplitFunc fit any bufio.Scanner the same way blevesearch's SplitWords does

gotchas: v2.1.0 and v2.1.1 are retracted in go.mod (surprising allocations). v2.5.0 changed FromString/FromBytes to return a pointer iterator, and v2 removed the Filter, Transform and All helpers, so code written for v1 needs rework.
words yields whitespace and punctuation tokens. Filtering to word-like tokens is now up to the caller, since the v1 Wordlike filter was removed.

FromReader inherits bufio.Scanner's 64 KiB default token limit, so a pathological grapheme or word longer than that (for example stacked combining marks) stops the scan with an error unless you call Buffer to raise it.

AnsiEscapeSequences8Bit reads C1 bytes 0x80-0x9F as controls. They are only checked at a token start, where valid UTF-8 never has a continuation byte, so valid text is unaffected, but mixed-encoding input will tokenize differently with it on.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It is the only Go segmenter in the category. Pick it for Go code, and pick cometkim/fast-grapheme-segmenter (Rust), unicode-segmenter (JavaScript), ugrapheme (Python) or uni-algo, libgrapheme and ICU (C/C++) in those languages. Its multilingual grapheme rate (245 MB/s on an M2) is in the same range as those siblings' own first-party numbers, but no shared harness compares them.
verified_claims_summary: First-party go test -bench on an Apple M2 (darwin/arm64, GOMAXPROCS 8), Go version unstated, single runs, from the in-repo comparative modules (local replace, so they measure HEAD-era code from February 2026). Graphemes are 14.2x (multilingual 34,962-byte sample) and 41.5x (4,500-byte ASCII) faster than rivo/uniseg v0.4.7's NewGraphemes, which also computes word, sentence, line and width state, so those ratios overstate a graphemes-only comparison. Words are 3.6x and 6.2x faster than blevesearch/segment v0.9.1. That baseline ran in its default build, the table-driven Ragel -T1 machine its README says is not the fastest; the -tags prod goto machine (-G2) was not used. Its loop also copies the input to []byte on every iteration, so the word ratios are upper bounds as well.
